study: WORKSTREAM A -- L5 source-mechanism autopsy from on-chain provenance

method.corpus: 763,966 L5 fills; 260 randomly sampled BTC15m windows, first 16 fills each -> 3,925 distinct transactions
method.provenance: eth_getTransactionReceipt on public Polygon RPCs; every fill classified from the EVENTS IN ITS OWN TRANSACTION. Nothing is inferred from price.
method.receipt_coverage: 2,739 / 3,925 (69.8%). Misses are RPC failures, not a class; they are reported as UNRECEIPTED and never imputed.
method.decoder_gap: March-April 2026 transactions run on a DIFFERENT exchange contract (0x4bfb41d5.., NegRisk) that this decoder does not read, so they classify as AMBIGUOUS. Mechanism rates are therefore quoted for MAY-AUGUST 2026 only, where ambiguity is 0.0%.

event_signatures_verified.computed_with: keccak256 of the canonical signatures, not recalled

headline.L5_NEVER_MINTS: Across every split/merge/redeem in 118 fully-audited fill transactions the PositionSplit stakeholder is 0xada100874d00e3331d00f2007a9c336a65009718 -- an operator contract, never L5's own address. Zero PositionsMerge and zero PayoutRedemption appear in his FILL transactions (redemption is a separate settlement transaction and is out of this sample by construction).
headline.so_minting_is_venue_plumbing: L5 posts ordinary limit orders. The venue mints a complete set to pair him with a buyer of the OPPOSITE outcome.

evolution.reading: L5 moved from taker-heavy to almost entirely mint-matched maker over four months. The mature form is the one to replicate.

the_26_percent_at_or_above_ask_RESOLVED.old_claim: 26.4% of L5 maker fills price at or above the contemporaneous best ask, 'which a resting bid cannot do', attributed to minting via a 1.5%-vs-99.86% feasibility discriminator
the_26_percent_at_or_above_ask_RESOLVED.what_the_chain_shows: all 118 audited fills are MAKER on-chain, taker share 0%, INCLUDING all 32 at-or-above-ask fills. A PositionSplit is present in 84% of the at/above-ask transactions AND 76% of the resting-bid-consistent ones.
the_26_percent_at_or_above_ask_RESOLVED.so_the_old_discriminator_does_not_discri: mint FEASIBILITY inferred from the complement's bid separated the classes; actual on-chain minting does not. Minting is the dominant mechanism for BOTH.
the_26_percent_at_or_above_ask_RESOLVED.the_actual_explanation: a mint-matched fill never touches L5's own ask ladder. His YES bid is paired with a NO BUYER and the operator mints the pair, so the YES best ask is irrelevant to that match and his fill price may sit at or above it without him ever crossing. The fills are genuine resting-order fills.

decisive_number.question: P(opposite ordinary-book fill within the window | ordinary first fill), BTC15m

rows.name: ANY first fill -> ANY opposite fill
BOOK-CROSS first -> BOOK-CROSS opposite  <-- THE STRICT NUMBER

decisive_number.answer: THE STRICT VERSION IS UNPOWERED, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING. Book crosses are only 5.5% of fills, so requiring BOTH legs to be book crosses yields n=4 in 260 windows (50% within window). It does not collapse to a low rate -- it collapses to NO SAMPLE. L5's recycling runs on mint-matching: MINT-MATCHED first -> MINT-MATCHED opposite is n=166 at 87.3% within window, 42.2%/66.3%/77.7% at 30/60/120s, median 32s.

does_it_transfer.verdict: YES. Mint-matching is not a resource we lack.
does_it_transfer.argument: On Polymarket the two outcomes are separate CTF tokens with separate books, so a YES buyer and a NO buyer CANNOT meet without the operator minting. On a single-ladder venue (Gemini, PMUS) a NO bid at n IS a YES ask at (1-n): the same two participants meet directly on one book. The counterparty set is identical; only the venue's bookkeeping differs.
does_it_transfer.measured_support: bid_Up + bid_Down over 17,102 joined L2 snapshots has median 0.990 -- the 1c spread split across two books -- and reaches >= 1.00 (mint feasible at the touch) in only 4.8% of them. So most mints are triggered by an ARRIVING order that lifts the sum to $1, i.e. an aggressor. On one ladder that same aggressor simply crosses our quote.
does_it_transfer.what_does_NOT_transfer: the arrival RATE of that counterparty. That is the habitat finding, unchanged.
does_it_transfer.caveat: this is a structural argument plus L2 measurement, not a controlled experiment. It would be falsified if a single-ladder venue were shown to route complement buyers somewhere other than the book.

l5_pair_economics_full_corpus.reading: BTC15m is the business: ~900 matched contracts a window at a median 0.968 basis with only 7.3% left as residual. BTC5m is far worse on every axis and should not be the transfer target.
